questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct for multilevel logic?
options: A multilevel logic representation will always produce a minimum delay between the input and the output.
As the number of levels in a multilevel logic increases, the delay between the input and the output decreases.
A multilevel logic can be transformed to explore various delay-area trade-offs.
A multilevel logic representation cannot be transformed into a two-level logic representation.
questions.accepted: A multilevel logic can be transformed to explore various delay-area trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the algebraic model in multilevel logic optimization is incorrect?
options: An algebraic model neglects some Boolean properties of the local functions.
An algebraic model treats a variable and its complement as separate variables.
Efficient algorithms can be designed to carry out division in an algebraic model.
An algebraic model can reduce the Boolean expression (a + a') to 1
questions.accepted: An algebraic model can reduce the Boolean expression (a + a') to 1

questions.prompt: A minterm is found to be Don't Care (DC) during logic optimization. Which of the following statements best describes the behavior of the logic synthesis tool?
options: A logic synthesis tool will implement a circuit that can produce either 0 or 1 for this minterm, depending on which of these values reduces the cost.
A logic synthesis tool will implement a circuit that always produces 0 for this minterm.
A logic synthesis tool will implement a circuit that always produces 1 for this minterm.
A logic synthesis tool will implement a circuit that always produces high impedance (Z value) for this minterm.
questions.accepted: A logic synthesis tool will implement a circuit that can produce either 0 or 1 for this minterm, depending on which of these values reduces the cost.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect for a typical sequential circuit implementation of a finite state machine (FSM)
options: The combination of the Q-pin value of flip-flops represents states.
The transition function is implemented using combinational logic.
Reducing the number of states in an FSM can never reduce the size of the circuit implementation.
State minimization and optimal state encoding can reduce the size of the circuit implementation.
questions.accepted: Reducing the number of states in an FSM can never reduce the size of the circuit implementation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect about state minimization in a finite state machine (FSM)
options: State minimization attempts to derive an FSM with the minimum number of states and exhibiting the same behavior as the original FSM.
State minimization can reduce the number of flip-flops in FSM implementation.
State minimization relies on retaining any one of the equivalent states and removing others.
State minimization will change the functionality/behavior of an FSM and should not be done.
questions.accepted: State minimization will change the functionality/behavior of an FSM and should not be done.

questions.prompt: Which of the following state encoding schemes for a finite state machine (FSM) reserves one bit for each state?
options: One-hot Encoding
Binary Encoding
Gray Encoding
Zero-shot Encoding

questions.prompt: Which of the following pairs of states are equivalent in the finite state machine (FSM) whose state diagram is shown below?

image.alt: State diagram with states sA, sB and sC: sA to sB labelled B/0, sB to sA labelled A/0, sB to itself labelled B/1, sA to sC labelled A/1, sC to sA labelled A/1, and sC to sB labelled B/0.

options: sA and sB
sA and sC
sB and sC
None of the states are equivalent

questions.prompt: Formal verification techniques rely on the following:
options: Simulation
Mathematical Proof
Random Guesses
Statistical Inference

questions.prompt: A Reduced Ordered Binary Decision Diagram (ROBDD) of a Boolean function:
options: Is a canonical representation
Is the same as a truth table
Always represents a Boolean function compactly.
Has size independent of the variable order

questions.prompt: What can we say about the Reduced Ordered Binary Decision Diagram (ROBDD) representation of a Boolean function f = ab(a' + b') (where a and b are Boolean variables)?
options: It will contain one non-terminal vertex and two leaf terminals.
It will contain two non-terminal vertex and two leaf terminals.
It will contain only one leaf terminal with the label 1
It will contain only one leaf terminal with the label 0
questions.accepted: It will contain only one leaf terminal with the label 0
